bb42c4d16c: Armitage Ghost Mural evokes the architectural identity of the Armitage-Halsted Landmark District. Its materials and design reference the neighborhood’s history as one of Chicago’s first-generation commercial districts.
5c7bb9d2cc: This mural was painted on the back wall of a new bike corral at the Lunt Ave. entrance of the Morse EL station on the CTA Red line. The theme for the wall was a general call for Bicycle Transportation, and artist Bruno Carneiro Mosciaro, aka Bruno Big, an artist based in Rio De Janeiro, won the commission. In "Bike-­?Family", Bruno Big approached the theme of using Bicycles as a collective joyful experience and integrating people with the environment and among themselves. The idea of depicting a family riding a bicycle is also a way of transforming the model of families owning a car and this being the main source of transportation and demonstrating that the act of riding a bicycle can be fun. Bruno Big works in a variety of media and is known for his vibrant colors and large forms that capture the subtle poetry of motion, the vivid pulse of life, and the dark mystery of death.
a9646512ac: The mural is an allegory of freedom and the teaching of love. It represents traveling souls, migration, and the home we all carry. The birds I depicted on the wall are endemic to Mexico's northern Pacific coast; they are called the beautiful black-throated magpie. I am inspired by nature, especially birds, because of what they symbolize: diversity, identity, and freedom.
